findings.what: verifyTyped still calls verifyGauntlet without requireSignature:true, so a forged unsigned ok:true record still satisfies this typed-success gate.
findings.why: The programmatic API defaults requireSignature off, and this caller is a live trust-boundary gate, not just a legacy shape unit test. I reproduced verifyTyped returning ok:true/status ran for an unsigned well-formed ok:true record.

findings.what: SIGNED_FIELDS still omits gauntlet decision fields sprint_id and started_at while gauntlet-verify reads them for correlation/window membership.
findings.why: A signed old record can be edited from sprint_id SP-OLD to SP-NEW and verifyRecord still returns true; verifyGauntlet with sprintId SP-NEW and requireSignature:true returns ok:true. Likewise, a signed started_at-only record can have started_at moved into the window without invalidating the signature.
